candidate.title: 5-C
candidate.scope: The single middle workflow labelled 5-C and Chromatin conformation capture carbon copy (5-C) in the supplied poster crop. Extract crosslinking, sample fragmentation, proximity ligation and the broad T7/T3-labelled ligation-mediated amplification block ending in DNA. The UMI-4C row above, PB-seq row below and clipped earlier-row captions are context, not alternative targets or connected branches. The matched 2007 5C protocol abstract clarifies the 3C-template/ligated-primer-library interface; no full text was supplied or inspected. This is a schematic architecture, not a complete protocol or an assertion that all 5C implementations are identical.

states.label: 5C DNA library of amplified ligated primers
features: The final DNA icon is a continuous red–teal–brown–green line after the LMA arrow.

The primary abstract identifies the library as ligated primers representing 3C ligation junctions; the readout carrier is therefore a DNA primer product rather than the original protein-bound chromatin.
In the sequencing use described by the catalogue, product identities report selected pairs of captured genomic fragments and can yield a matrix of interaction frequencies.

Coverage depends on chosen targets and prior sequence information. Captured junctions can include random chromosomal collisions, so detection alone does not establish a functional regulatory interaction or a precise physical contact position.

operations.description: Convert the starting chromatin contact into a crosslinked DNA–protein complex, shown by the newly added red cross marks. The primary abstract identifies formaldehyde as the crosslinking reagent.
operations.information_effect: Retains spatial association between DNA regions in a protein-associated complex for subsequent fragmentation and ligation.

operations.label: Sample fragmentation
operations.description: Cut the crosslinked chromatin DNA into fragments. The output retains two short DNA regions together with the crosslinked blue protein; fragmentation does not itself remove the association. Restriction digestion is the primary-supported implementation of this generic caption.
operations.mechanism: Restriction-enzyme digestion of crosslinked chromatin, without assigning an enzyme or detailed end structure.
operations.information_effect: Places the retained contact on discrete genomic fragments that can subsequently be joined.

operations.label: Ligation
operations.description: Join DNA fragments held in the crosslinked complex into a continuous DNA contact product. The protein and red cross marks remain in this cartoon, while the previously separate colored DNA segments are now joined near the pale-yellow rectangle.
operations.mechanism: Ligation of crosslinked DNA fragments; the abstract reports that the implementation promotes intramolecular ligation.
operations.information_effect: Converts captured spatial proximity into a covalent DNA junction. Such a junction supports detection of a captured association, not by itself its biological function.

operations.label: LMA: Ligation-mediated amplification
operations.description: The depicted route takes the proximity-ligated DNA product into a protein-free DNA cartoon with T7/T3-labelled oligonucleotides, then yields the final multicolored DNA product. At this broad block's entrance, the primary abstract specifies purification of the ligation products to a 3C library; purification is an unshown interface, not a separately depicted operation. Interpret the opposing primer segments as recognizing the two joined DNA regions, so a ligated-primer product represents that junction and is amplified. The 3C DNA acts as template; the primers supply the library product. Keep this as one LMA block because the figure does not separate its internal reactions.
operations.mechanism: Highly multiplexed ligation-mediated amplification of 3C ligation junctions, producing a library of ligated primers. The schematic shows T7 and T3 primer labels without defining additional chemistry.
operations.information_effect: Transfers selected contact-junction identities from the purified 3C DNA template into amplified ligated-primer DNA products. Sequencing those products can identify captured pairs among the selected regions. Sequencing and computation are not drawn as separate operations; the abstract's microarray option is not another target workflow in this poster row.

checks.rationale: The final multicolored DNA icon supports a DNA output, and the primary abstract identifies its carrier as ligated primers detecting 3C junctions. The candidate distinguishes this proxy from the original protein-associated DNA. Selected fragment-pair identities and a matrix of interaction frequencies are consistent with that junction readout and the catalogue; prior target information and random-collision limitations are supported. Its statement that the spatial contact position is not precisely established is an explicit inference from fragment-based capture, not a denial that sequencing can resolve the ligated fragment sequence. Microarray detection is mentioned only as abstract context and is not added as a depicted branch.

evidence.quote: Ligation products are subsequently purified to generate a 3C library.
